description: "Workflow as tool": WRITE-capable tools over the Dagster instance (materialize_assets, run_job) for agents -- each a real, synchronous dagster.execute_job run, not a read-only query. Registers a resource and ships a stdio MCP server (python -m <module>) for agentic_pipeline's tool_use_loop / mcp_call. A deliberately separate component from the read-only dagster_instance_tools.

resource_key.label: Resource Key
resource_key.description: Resource key the toolset is registered under

definitions_module.label: Definitions Module
definitions_module.description: Required 'pkg.module[:attr]' that yields the Definitions this tool is allowed to materialize/run (attr defaults to `defs`). Unlike dagster_instance_tools (read-only), a write tool must know its own scope -- there is no 'degrade gracefully without it' mode here.

allow.label: Allow
allow.description: Hard allow-list of tools (default: all). Valid: materialize_assets, run_job.

allow_assets.label: Allow Assets
allow_assets.description: Hard allow-list of asset keys materialize_assets may target (default: any asset in definitions_module). Recommended in production -- an agent should materialize specific, intended assets, not anything in the repo.

allow_jobs.label: Allow Jobs
allow_jobs.description: Hard allow-list of job names run_job may target (default: any job in definitions_module).

default_tags.label: Default Tags
default_tags.description: Tags merged onto every triggered run, alongside dagster-community/workflow-tool=true (e.g. {'triggered_by': 'support-agent'}) -- for run-tag attribution/audit.

mcp_server_resource_key.label: Mcp Server Resource Key
mcp_server_resource_key.description: If set, ALSO registers a stdio MCP-server-shaped resource (same name/type/command/env shape as MCPServerResource) under this key, built from this component's own settings -- python -m this module, with the DAGSTER_WORKFLOW_TOOLS_* env vars set from definitions_module/allow/allow_assets/allow_jobs/default_tags. DAGSTER_HOME (and anything listed in mcp_extra_env_vars) is read fresh from the environment at run time (when a consumer actually resolves this resource), not baked in at component load. Any mcp_servers-aware component (mcp_tool_call, mcp_tool_picker, the agent components, agentic_pipeline) can then reference it via server_resource_key instead of hand-writing an inline command+env entry. Leave unset to skip this -- existing resource_key-only behavior is unchanged.

mcp_extra_env_vars.label: Mcp Extra Env Vars
mcp_extra_env_vars.description: mcp_server_resource_key only. Extra env var NAMES to copy (their current value, read fresh every time a consumer resolves the resource -- same run-time timing as DAGSTER_HOME) from this process into the spawned MCP server's env. MCP's stdio client does not inherit the rest of the environment, so anything your Dagster instance's own config needs beyond DAGSTER_HOME -- e.g. a Dagster+ agent's DAGSTER_CLOUD_AGENT_LABEL -- must be listed here, or the spawned server crashes at startup trying to resolve its instance. Note: a Dagster+ agent's own DAGSTER_HOME is its own agent process's home, not necessarily where you want triggered runs to land -- decide which instance this server should actually launch runs through before pointing it at an agent's env.

inspection_asset_name.label: Inspection Asset Name
inspection_asset_name.description: If set, ALSO emits a declare-only asset by this name with the allowed tool names + descriptions as metadata (tool_names, tool_descriptions, tool_count) -- the toolset is fixed Python code, not a configurable server, so this never materializes; it just makes the tool list catalog-visible without a UI having to spawn the MCP server to ask. `allowed_tools` (on agentic_pipeline's tool_use_loop, and the agent components) matches against '<mcp_servers: entry name>__<tool>' -- for the mcp_server_resource_key path, that name is whatever `mcp_server_resource_key` itself is set to.

graphql_url.label: Graphql Url
graphql_url.description: GraphQL endpoint for launch_job (e.g. 'http://localhost:3000/graphql' for a local OSS webserver, or your Dagster+ deployment's GraphQL URL). Required to enable launch_job -- there is no implicit default, since a Dagster+ URL is always org/deployment-specific. Leave unset to skip launch_job entirely (materialize_assets/run_job are unaffected).

graphql_api_token_env_var.label: Graphql Api Token Env Var
graphql_api_token_env_var.description: Env var holding a Dagster+ user/API token, sent as the 'Dagster-Cloud-Api-Token' header on the launch_job GraphQL request. Leave unset for a local OSS webserver with no auth configured.

repository_location_name.label: Repository Location Name
repository_location_name.description: Code location name launch_job's GraphQL selector targets -- required to enable launch_job (the name this code location is loaded under: dagster_cloud.yaml's 'location_name', or the module/package name for a plain OSS workspace.yaml entry).

repository_name.label: Repository Name
repository_name.description: Repository name within that code location, for launch_job's GraphQL selector. '__repository__' (the default) is Dagster's own name for the implicit single repository every plain `Definitions` object becomes (verified directly against dagster-webserver's own buildRepoPathForURL) -- only override if you explicitly built a named @repository.

job_owners.label: Job Owners
job_owners.description: {job_name: [owners]} -- launch_job's authorization source for a job with no asset metadata to check (a non-asset job, or one you want to authorize separately from its assets' own owners). An asset job's owners are read LIVE from its own assets' `owners` catalog metadata instead and don't need an entry here. Same email / 'team:<name>' convention as every owners: field in this repo -- team: entries never authorize a launch_job call (no group-membership check). A job with neither an asset-owners source nor an entry here can never be launched via launch_job.

requester_template.label: Requester Template
requester_template.description: mcp_server_resource_key only. A template string -- typically '{tag.<key>}', e.g. '{tag.slack/user}' -- passed through VERBATIM as this spawned server's DAGSTER_WORKFLOW_TOOLS_REQUESTER env value. This component never resolves the placeholder itself; the CALLING agent component's own generic {tag.*} substitution (applied to every mcp_servers[].env value at run time) resolves it from a real run tag right before spawning the subprocess -- so launch_job's requester identity always comes from a trusted, server-side source, never a model-settable tool argument. For an inline (non-shared) mcp_servers entry instead, just set env.DAGSTER_WORKFLOW_TOOLS_REQUESTER directly in the agent's own YAML -- this field only matters when sharing this component's own mcp_server_resource_key.
